none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex quadratic minimization: f(x)=½ E[⟨a,x−u⟩²], with minimum f(u)=0. The covariance may be singular; no positive lower eigenvalue or strong convexity is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,a)=⟨a,x−u⟩a using a fresh IID sample. This is an unbiased gradient of f. Only the gradient vector is returned; neither the sample a nor a function value is provided. L and x0 are public; R, ε, δ, u, and the sampling distribution are hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is exactly two-dimensional real Euclidean space with its standard inner product.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Realizable least squares with bounded features: ‖a‖²≤L almost surely. Every sample loss has the common minimizer u, so stochastic gradients vanish at u. Sample Hessians aaᵀ have operator norm at most L, and f is L-smooth. The gradient noise is state-dependent, with E‖g(x,a)−∇f(x)‖²≤2Lf(x); no globally uniform variance bound is assumed. The initial point satisfies ‖x0−u‖≤R. Valid parameters obey L,R,ε>0 and 0<δ<1.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and satisfy f(output)−f(u)≤ε outside the allowed failure event, for some global minimizer u. No particular iterate or averaging rule is prescribed.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: P(f(output)−f(u)>ε)≤δ, equivalently success probability at least 1−δ. In Template.Convergence, this probability includes algorithm randomness and oracle randomness.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is realizable population least-squares minimization with bounded IID features, stochastic gradients, and a high-probability objective-gap target, an established stochastic optimization formulation. Least-squares stochastic approximation is treated in [Bach and Moulines (2013)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2013/file/7fe1f8abaad094e0b5cb1b01d712f708-Paper.pdf). No proved results or extracted budgets were supplied, so no complexity comparison is reported.
